assumptions.summary: School educational statistics remain constant over five years.
Every received dollar is spent to improve student performance.
Social utility is concave and represented by a logarithm.
Funding supply is used reluctantly as a focus proxy because demand is unavailable.
Existing other investment is set to x0=0 because data are limited.
k balances earnings and graduation-rate components.
Allocations below 1000 dollars are operationally useless and set to zero.

Bind school stability, fund-to-performance, concavity, x0=0, no discount, and solver premises to the local source and consequence.
Version focus indicators, state exclusions, school identifiers, imputation masks, PCA matrices, earnings/graduation inputs, existing grants, and allocation outputs.
Exclude office fields, Contents, formula-only blocks, table cells, captions, References, and the source-attributed appendix from positive author prose.
State source, population, year, direction, unit, missingness, transform, decision role, and downstream consumer before interpretation.
Separate focus screening, PCA, utility, dynamic ROI, KKT formulation, hybrid solver, postprocessing, and sensitivity as typed model units.
Keep school state, utility, yearly ROI, cumulative objective, budget feasibility, optimizer fitness, and recommendation rank distinct.
Preflight school counts, top-50/top-500 handoff, dimensions, baseline investment, annual sums, duration, k, and optimizer settings.
Do not add investment dollars directly to an earnings/graduation composite without a dimensional and response model.
Treat ranking overlap, one fitness curve, budget utilization, and one-way k sensitivity as bounded internal checks.
Report PCA matrices, loadings, utility calibration, existing grants, solver settings, seeds, restarts, residuals, raw allocations, and uncertainty.
Repeat screening, utility, baseline, horizon, solver, rounding, and sensitivity checks across declared alternatives and tolerances.
Label every score, ROI, investment amount, duration, utilization, comparator, and sensitivity result by unit, year, scenario, and evidence status.
Trace each school allocation through mission authority, beneficiaries, state filters, alternatives, feasibility, uncertainty, monitoring, and correction.
Trace each recommendation through the concrete difficulty, disclosed fallback, mathematical transformation, visual/result reading, and bounded action.
Retain all 27 pages, five figures, numbered and appendix tables, main/appendix formulas, flow chart, convergence curve, and full recommendation list.
Retain self-objection before downgrade, failed-method switching, unit-problem disclosure, algorithm-before-table order, and stakeholder translation.

Preserve handoffs from mission to filter, data to PCA, school state to utility, yearly ROI to endpoint objective, constraints to solver, and output to CFO.
Do not treat adding donations to a cross-sectional school-state index as a causal response without identification and follow-up outcomes.
Keep paper-internal task reconstruction separate from unavailable official wording and preserve every excluded or source-attributed region.

data_and_preprocessing.summary: Inputs are split into school-selection/focus data and ROI data.
FC1000 subject and location distributions are used to infer existing capital supply.
Manual selection excludes NY, CA, DC, and MA; 2,977 institutions become 2,323.
PCA uses 68 indicators with mean fill and standardization.
Components are retained to 90 percent cumulative contribution.
Prose alternates between top 50 and top 500 before later optimizing 50 schools.
Earnings, graduates, graduation rate, k, and investment enter utility.
The full recommendation table contains 50 schools and annual amounts.

dependency_graph.handoff: The focus filter supplies the school population and indicator matrix to PCA.
The screened candidate set supplies school states to utility construction.
Successive utility states define yearly ROI and the telescoped objective.
The endpoint objective and annual budget become the constrained allocation problem.
The KKT formulation is handed to the attributed hybrid numerical solver.
The solver vector is rounded, ranked, and published as a recommendation.
The recommendation is compared with external lists and rerun under k perturbations.

independent_extensions.summary: Acquire demand and financing-gap data before using grant supply as need.
Release missingness masks, PCA matrices, loadings, scores, threshold alternatives, and screening recall.
Build a dimensionally valid response model with existing grants and observed education outcomes.
Use an objective that retains timing if duration is a decision.
Model minimum grants inside the constraints so rounding preserves feasibility.
Release code, hyperparameters, seeds, restarts, residuals, objective bounds, and solver comparisons.
Replace overlap rhetoric with declared metrics and beneficiary-level duplication data.
Run multi-parameter uncertainty and decision-stability analysis.
Audit every duration and annual amount against the five-year horizon and top-table copy.
Validate recommendations against realized student outcomes and stakeholder-defined equity.

judge_relevance_hypotheses.summary: The supply-demand self-objection makes the evidence downgrade unusually explicit.
The all-funds counterfactual gives the concave utility a concrete decision reason.
Two failed methods make the hybrid switch readable rather than decorative.
The algorithm appears before the allocation table and exposes postprocessing.
The CFO letter retains the marginal-utility mechanism while reducing notation.

language_observations.summary: Reusable human writing moves center on a self-objection before downgrade, candid method failure before switching, unit-gap disclosure, algebra-to-decision handoffs, practical postprocessing, and a mechanism-bearing CFO translation.
the Summary compresses the five-year allocation route: Move from school selection through utility, incremental ROI, constrained optimization, allocation, and sensitivity.
computational pressure triggers staged data reduction: Explain why thousands of schools and contest-time computing require selection before optimization.
the planned approach names inputs, actions, and outputs: Give each of three parts its data, operation, and downstream deliverable.
a supply-only inference is self-refuted before reluctant reuse: Read the funding chart, object that supply omits demand, disclose unavailable demand data, and narrow the claim.
the charity concern is converted into a focus filter: Translate mission priorities into indicator groups and manual exclusions before PCA.
data are split by downstream consumer: Separate focus/selection inputs from ROI inputs before transformation.
PCA is narrated as a selection ladder: Move from mean fill through standardization, eigendecomposition, cumulative contribution, and ranking.
the preliminary ranking is explicitly separated from recommendation: Warn that PCA rank lacks ROI before passing candidates to strategy making.
a pathological allocation motivates concave utility: Reject linear or convex utility because it concentrates all funds, then choose a log function.
unequal utility components trigger a balancing constant: Name the unit mismatch between earnings and graduation rate before introducing k.
missing prior investment is converted into an explicit zero: Disclose limited data, set x0 to zero, and continue the recurrence.
yearly ROI is telescoped to an endpoint objective: Write yearly utility differences, cancel intermediate terms, and retain yearly constraints.
failed KKT and ordinary PSO attempts trigger a hybrid solver: Name theoretical feasibility, programming scale, failed attempt, slow convergence, and the next method.
a source-attributed algorithm is made inspectable by a flow chart: Expose multiplier, swarm, conjugate-gradient, and two stopping loops while retaining attribution.
one fitness curve is read as convergence evidence: Describe the early drop and flattening before reporting the solution.
practical postprocessing modifies the computed allocation: Call tiny grants useless, set them to zero, and report utilization above 99 percent.
the decision rule precedes the allocation table: State optimizer and units before publishing ranked school-year amounts.
external rankings are used as bounded comparisons: Count overlaps with PCA and Gates lists before interpreting agreement or nonduplication.
one balancing parameter is perturbed before a robustness claim: Vary k, report investment dispersion, and call the effect bearable.
the conclusion is translated into a CFO mechanism: Explain diminishing marginal utility, target schools, five-year allocation, and adjustable k without most notation.

The five yearly utility differences telescope to final minus initial utility.
KKT and ordinary PSO are abandoned for the attributed LA_PSO_GT hybrid.
One fitness trace flattens near 50 iterations.

k sensitivity reports investment standard deviations under plus/minus 5 and 10 percent.

source.title: The Optimal Investment Strategy Based on the Large-scale Non-linear Constraint Optimization Methods

source_quality.summary: All 27 pages were read in order and visually reviewed. The paper moves from a charitable focus and computational screening pressure through PCA, a log-utility state, incremental ROI, endpoint reduction, KKT/PSO method switching, an attributed hybrid optimizer, practical rounding, five-year recommendations, external comparison, one-way sensitivity, explicit weaknesses, and a CFO handoff.

decisions: which schools to consider, how to value marginal educational benefit, how much to invest each year, how long to fund, and how to communicate uncertainty
inputs: educational institution data, external grant-supply distributions, foundation priorities, 100M annual budget, five-year horizon
outputs: focus filter, PCA ranking, social utility and ROI, 50-school annual allocation, duration, sensitivity and CFO recommendation

title: The Optimal Investment Strategy Based on the Large-scale Non-linear Constraint Optimization Methods
unresolved_questions: Summary top-50, body top-500, and later 50-school optimization counts are inconsistent.
Constant school statistics for five years and omission of discounting are unsupported.
The assumption that all received funding improves student performance is not identified from outcomes.
Lower Pell-grant share appears as a focus criterion despite the stated poverty mission; direction needs clarification.
Excluding NY, CA, DC, and MA uses a supply-only policy premise after the paper admits demand data are missing.
Mean imputation is claimed not to affect results without missingness diagnostics or sensitivity.
PCA loadings, eigenvalues, component weights, and a threshold sensitivity analysis are absent.
The screening index has no causal or construct-validation bridge to donation outcomes.
Earnings, graduation rate, and dollar investments enter one logarithm without a consistent dimensional ledger.
The balancing constant k has no database, elicitation protocol, or uncertainty distribution.
Setting x0=0 ignores existing foundation and government investment that the paper itself discusses.
Cross-sectional school statistics are treated as donation-response state variables without causal identification.
Telescoping removes intermediate timing from the objective and weakens the claimed duration strategy.
Zeroing small allocations makes every reported yearly utilization below 100 percent and violates the original equality constraints.
KKT theory and one fitness curve do not demonstrate reproducible convergence or global optimality.
LA_PSO_GT is explicitly source-attributed; originality and implementation fidelity must remain separate.
The allocation evidence does not establish that a heuristic local/global search found the shared-budget global optimum.
Two PCA-list overlaps do not establish correlation and zero Gates-list overlap does not prove nonduplication.
Sensitivity varies only k and reports investment standard deviation without utility loss, rank stability, or a decision threshold.
The full recommendation table contains duration values that appear incompatible with the stated five-year horizon.
No executable code, seed, swarm settings, restart study, raw trace, or uncertainty propagation is released.
Claims that the method applies broadly to nonlinear constrained problems exceed this single heuristic application.

visualization_observations.next_action: Treat sub-100 percent sums as a constraint violation, not exact feasibility.

visualization_observations.next_action: Do not infer nonduplication or broad robustness.

visualization_observations.next_action: Audit every duration, annual sum, unit, and top-table match.

visualization_observations.next_action: Separate author application from borrowed exposition and release executable fidelity evidence.
